// purpose: @debuggen/shared - the compiler project for the monorepo typecheck gate. `pnpm typecheck` (= `pnpm demo:generate && tsc -b`) builds the root solution file, which lists this project first because packages/shared is the bottom of the acyclic package graph (AAP 0.2.2): it depends on no other workspace, so nothing here may declare project `references`.
// format: Strict JSON, like tsconfig.base.json and every other tsconfig in this repository: both a JSONC-aware reader (`ts.readConfigFile`) and a bare `JSON.parse` can read it, so no consumer has to know which one to reach for. tsc, ESLint, Vitest, tsup and Prettier all accept comments in a tsconfig, but the rationale for each decision is recorded in the `"// …"` string keys of this object instead. TypeScript ignores unknown TOP-LEVEL keys, which is what makes the convention safe; a `"// …"` key inside `compilerOptions` is a hard error instead (TS5023, "Unknown compiler option"), so every note about a single option lives up here under a `"// compilerOptions.<option>"` key and never beside the option itself.
// inherited: Everything that is not stated below is inherited from tsconfig.base.json and must stay that way - in particular `strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `verbatimModuleSyntax`, `isolatedModules`, the no-unused/no-implicit diagnostics, `target`/`lib` ES2023, and the declaration-emit settings (`declaration`, `declarationMap`, `sourceMap`, `emitDeclarationOnly`, `incremental`). `noEmit` must never be added: TypeScript 6.0.3 rejects a referenced project that disables emit with TS6310 and the whole gate fails.
// compilerOptions.composite: Already true in the base; restated because the root solution file references this project and a non-composite reference fails `tsc -b` outright (TS6306). Keeping it local means a future edit to the base cannot silently break the gate at this project.
// compilerOptions.module: The base defaults to "ESNext" + "bundler" for the bundled/web workspaces and instructs Node-targeted projects - naming the `./node` entry of this package - to override with NodeNext. package.json declares `"type": "module"`, and the `./node` export (dist/node/index.js) is loaded directly by Node in the local service and the telemetry preload, so this project is type-checked under real Node ESM resolution instead of a bundler approximation. Consequence for every source file in src/**: relative specifiers must carry an explicit ".js" extension (`export * from "./ids.js"`), and directory specifiers must name the file (`"./node/index.js"`). Extensionless relative imports are a compile error here by design - they would break real Node consumers of dist/node/index.js. tsup/esbuild resolve a "./x.js" specifier from a TypeScript importer back to "./x.ts", so the bundles are unaffected.
// compilerOptions.rootDir: Per-workspace (the base deliberately leaves it unset), so the declaration tree under .tsbuild/ mirrors src/ exactly: src/index.ts -> .tsbuild/index.d.ts and src/node/index.ts -> .tsbuild/node/index.d.ts, matching the paths the package.json `exports` map advertises under dist/.
// compilerOptions.types: The base sets no `types` so that one workspace's ambient globals cannot bleed into another. This package needs exactly one: @types/node 24.13.6 (a root devDependency, resolved through the workspace-root node_modules/@types). It types the `node:crypto` / `node:fs` / `node:path` builtins used by src/node/** and also declares the cross-platform globals the root entry relies on (`crypto.getRandomValues`, `performance`). Deliberately no "lib": ["DOM"] override: the root entry is imported by browser bundles *and* by Node, so it must stay on globals that exist in both. Adding DOM would legitimise `window`/`document` in a package that also runs in the service and the preload.
// compilerOptions.not-overridden: NOT overridden: "outDir" / "declarationDir" / "tsBuildInfoFile". The base already anchors them per project with `${configDir}`, which resolves to the directory of THIS file, so declarations and the incremental stamp land in packages/shared/.tsbuild (ignored by .gitignore and .prettierignore). tsc must never write into packages/shared/dist: that directory belongs to tsup and holds the artefacts the `exports` map points at. NOT overridden: "skipLibCheck" (the base already enables it), and no strictness flag is relaxed or added on top of the base.
// include: src/** only, and deliberately including the colocated `*.test.ts` files so the typecheck gate covers the tests too. They import `{ describe, it, expect }` from "vitest" explicitly rather than relying on globals, and vitest resolves from the workspace-root node_modules, so no "vitest/globals" entry is needed in `types`.
// exclude: Replaces the base's inherited list; resolved relative to this directory, so it means packages/shared/dist and packages/shared/node_modules. Belt and braces: `include` already restricts the input set to src/**, and the tsup output in dist/ plus the declaration output in .tsbuild/ sit outside it.
// references: No "files" array and no "references": this project owns src/** wholesale and imports no other workspace.
